case.question: On a certain satellite channel, the sender transmits frames with a length of 512B from one direction, and the data transmission rate of the sender is 64kb/s. The receiver at the other end returns a very short acknowledgment frame. Given that the one-way propagation delay of the satellite channel from end to end is 270 ms, what is the throughput of the channel for sending window sizes of 1, 7, 17, and 117, respectively?

response.content:
The transmission time for one 512-byte frame is

\[
T_f=\frac{512\times 8}{64{,}000}=0.064\text{ s}=64\text{ ms}.
\]

The acknowledgment returns after the round-trip propagation delay, so the acknowledgment cycle is

\[
T_{\text{cycle}}=T_f+2T_p=64+2(270)=604\text{ ms}=0.604\text{ s}.
\]

With sending window \(W\), up to \(W\) frames can be sent per cycle:

\[
\text{Throughput}=\min\left(64,\frac{W\times512\times8}{0.604}\right)\text{ kb/s}.
\]

Thus:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
W & \text{Throughput}\\
\hline
1 & 6.8\text{ kb/s}\\
7 & 47.5\text{ kb/s}\\
17 & 64\text{ kb/s (capped)}\\
117 & 64\text{ kb/s (capped)}
\end{array}
\]

This corresponds to choice C.

Answer: C
